455	    def parse(self) -> _Select:
456	        select = self._parse_select()
457	        if self._peek().kind != "eof":
458	            tok = self._peek()
459	            raise QuerySyntaxError(f"unexpected trailing input {tok.text!r}")
460	        return select
461	
462	    def _parse_select(self) -> _Select:
463	        self._expect_keyword("select")
464	        items = tuple(self._parse_projection())
465	        self._expect_keyword("from")
466	        table_tok = self._expect_table_name()
467	        join = None
468	        if self._allow_join:
469	            if self._accept_keyword("inner"):
470	                self._expect_keyword("join")
471	                join = self._parse_join("inner")
472	            elif self._accept_keyword("left"):
473	                self._expect_keyword("join")
474	                join = self._parse_join("left")
475	        where = None
476	        if self._accept_keyword("where"):
477	            where = self._parse_or()
478	        group_by = None
479	        if self._accept_keyword("group"):
480	            self._expect_keyword("by")
481	            names = [self._parse_group_name()]
482	            while self._accept_op(","):
483	                names.append(self._parse_group_name())
484	            group_by = tuple(names)
485	        order_by = None
486	        if self._accept_keyword("order"):
487	            self._expect_keyword("by")
488	            order_items = [self._parse_order_item()]
489	            while self._accept_op(","):
490	                order_items.append(self._parse_order_item())
491	            order_by = tuple(order_items)
492	        limit = None
493	        if self._accept_keyword("limit"):
494	            limit = self._parse_limit()
495	        return _Select(
496	            items=items,
497	            table=table_tok.value,
498	            table_quoted=table_tok.kind == "qident",
499	            where=where,
500	            group_by=group_by,
501	            order_by=order_by,
502	            limit=limit,
503	            join=join,
504	        )
505	
506	    def _parse_join(self, kind: str) -> _Join:
507	        table_tok = self._expect_table_name()
508	        self._expect_keyword("on")
509	        left_key = self._parse_on_key()
510	        self._expect_op("=")
511	        right_key = self._parse_on_key()
512	        return _Join(
513	            kind=kind,
514	            table=table_tok.value,
515	            table_quoted=table_tok.kind == "qident",
516	            left_key=left_key,
517	            right_key=right_key,
518	        )
519	
520	    def _parse_on_key(self) -> tuple:
521	        tok = self._peek()
522	        if tok.kind not in ("ident", "qident"):
523	            raise QuerySyntaxError(
524	                f"ON requires table-qualified columns, got {tok.text!r}"
525	            )
526	        self._next()
527	        if not self._accept_op("."):
528	            raise QuerySyntaxError(
529	                "ON requires table-qualified columns (table.column)"
530	            )
531	        nxt = self._peek()
532	        if nxt.kind not in ("ident", "qident"):
533	            raise QuerySyntaxError(
534	                f"expected column name after '.' in ON, got {nxt.text!r}"
535	            )
536	        self._next()
537	        return (tok.value, tok.kind == "qident", nxt.value)
538	
539	    def _parse_projection(self) -> list[_RefItem]:
540	        items = [self._parse_select_item()]
541	        while self._accept_op(","):
542	            items.append(self._parse_select_item())
543	        # Aliases are only supported for computed scalar expressions (which
544	        # consume their own "AS alias" in _parse_select_item); a trailing
545	        # identifier (including the spelling "as") where FROM is expected
546	        # names one on a bare column or aggregate.  Plain queries keep their
547	        # historical QuerySyntaxError classification; aggregate queries treat
548	        # the unsupported alias as a validation error.
549	        tok = self._peek()
550	        if tok.kind in ("ident", "qident") or (
551	            tok.kind == "keyword" and tok.value == "as"
552	        ):
553	            grouped_ahead = any(
554	                t.kind == "keyword" and t.value == "group"
555	                for t in self.tokens[self.pos :]
556	            )
557	            if any(item.kind == "agg" for item in items) or grouped_ahead:
558	                raise QueryValidationError(
559	                    f"aliases are not supported; unexpected {tok.text!r} after projection item"
560	                )
561	            raise QuerySyntaxError(f"expected FROM, got {tok.text!r}")
562	        return items
563	
564	    def _parse_select_item(self) -> _RefItem:
565	        tok = self._peek()
566	        if tok.kind == "star":
567	            self._next()
568	            return _RefItem("star")
569	        if (
570	            tok.kind == "ident"
571	            and tok.value.lower() in _AGG_NAMES
572	            and self.tokens[self.pos + 1].kind == "op"
573	            and self.tokens[self.pos + 1].value == "("
574	        ):
575	            item = self._parse_column_or_agg()
576	            if self._arith_op_ahead():
577	                raise QueryValidationError(
578	                    "aggregate calls cannot be combined with scalar arithmetic"
579	                )
580	            return item
581	        node = self._parse_arith()
582	        if node[0] == "column":
583	            # A bare (possibly parenthesised) column reference keeps its
584	            # existing projection behaviour and needs no alias.
585	            return _RefItem(
586	                "column", name=node[1], table=node[2], table_quoted=node[3]
587	            )
588	        # A computed scalar expression must be named with AS.
589	        self._expect_keyword("as")
590	        alias = self._peek()
591	        if alias.kind not in ("ident", "qident"):
592	            raise QuerySyntaxError(
593	                f"AS requires a result name, got {alias.text!r}"
594	            )
595	        self._next()
596	        return _RefItem("expr", name=alias.value, expr=node)
597	
598	    def _arith_op_ahead(self) -> bool:
599	        tok = self._peek()
600	        return tok.kind == "star" or (
601	            tok.kind == "op" and tok.value in ("+", "-", "/")
602	        )
603	
604	    def _parse_order_item(self) -> _RefItem:
605	        item = self._parse_column_or_agg()
606	        descending = False
607	        if self._accept_keyword("asc"):
608	            descending = False
609	        elif self._accept_keyword("desc"):
610	            descending = True
611	        nulls_first: bool | None = None
612	        if self._accept_keyword("nulls"):
613	            if self._accept_keyword("first"):
614	                nulls_first = True
615	            elif self._accept_keyword("last"):
616	                nulls_first = False
617	            else:
618	                tok = self._peek()
619	                raise QuerySyntaxError(
620	                    f"expected FIRST or LAST after NULLS, got {tok.text!r}"
621	                )
622	        return _RefItem(
623	            item.kind,
624	            name=item.name,
625	            func=item.func,
626	            arg=item.arg,
627	            descending=descending,
628	            nulls_first=nulls_first,
629	            table=item.table,
630	            table_quoted=item.table_quoted,
631	            arg_table=item.arg_table,
632	            arg_table_quoted=item.arg_table_quoted,
633	        )
634	
635	    def _qualifier_ahead(self) -> bool:
636	        nxt = self.tokens[self.pos + 1]
637	        return nxt.kind == "op" and nxt.value == "."
638	
639	    def _parse_qualified_column(self) -> _RefItem:
640	        # Current token starts "table.column"; consumes all three tokens.
641	        table_tok = self._next()
642	        self._expect_op(".")
643	        name_tok = self._peek()
644	        if name_tok.kind not in ("ident", "qident"):
645	            raise QuerySyntaxError(
646	                f"expected identifier after '.', got {name_tok.text!r}"
647	            )
648	        self._next()
649	        return _RefItem(
650	            "column",
651	            name=name_tok.value,
652	            table=table_tok.value,
653	            table_quoted=table_tok.kind == "qident",
654	        )
655	
656	    def _parse_column_or_agg(self) -> _RefItem:
657	        tok = self._peek()
658	        if tok.kind not in ("ident", "qident"):
659	            raise QuerySyntaxError(f"expected identifier, got {tok.text!r}")
660	        if self._allow_join and self._qualifier_ahead():
661	            return self._parse_qualified_column()
662	        # A quoted identifier, or a bare word not spelled like an aggregate,
663	        # can only be a plain column reference.
664	        if tok.kind == "qident" or tok.value.lower() not in _AGG_NAMES:
665	            self._next()
666	            return _RefItem("column", name=tok.value)
667	        func = tok.value.lower()
668	        self._next()  # consume the function name
669	        if not self._accept_op("("):
670	            # e.g. a column literally named "count" -- the name token is
671	            # already consumed, so it is a plain column reference.
672	            return _RefItem("column", name=tok.value)
673	        arg, arg_table, arg_table_quoted = self._parse_aggregate_args(func)
674	        self._expect_op(")")
675	        return _RefItem(
676	            "agg",
677	            func=func.upper(),
678	            arg=arg,
679	            arg_table=arg_table,
680	            arg_table_quoted=arg_table_quoted,
681	        )
682	
683	    def _parse_aggregate_args(self, func: str) -> tuple:
684	        # Exactly one argument: '*' for COUNT, otherwise one (possibly
685	        # table-qualified) identifier.  Returns (name, table, table_quoted);
686	        # name "" stands for '*'.
687	        tok = self._peek()
688	        if tok.kind == "keyword" and tok.value == "case":
689	            raise QueryValidationError(
690	                f"{func.upper()} argument must be a column reference, not a CASE expression"
691	            )
692	        if tok.kind == "star":
693	            if func != "count":
694	                raise QuerySyntaxError(f"{func.upper()} does not accept '*'")
695	            self._next()
696	            return ("", None, False)
697	        if tok.kind not in ("ident", "qident"):
698	            raise QuerySyntaxError(
699	                f"{func.upper()} requires one column argument, got {tok.text!r}"
700	            )
701	        if self._allow_join and self._qualifier_ahead():
702	            item = self._parse_qualified_column()
703	            nxt = self._peek()
704	            if nxt.kind == "op" and nxt.value == "(":
705	                raise QuerySyntaxError(
706	                    f"{func.upper()} argument must be a column name, not a function call"
707	                )
708	            self._reject_expression_in_agg_arg(func)
709	            return (item.name, item.table, item.table_quoted)
710	        self._next()
711	        nxt = self._peek()
712	        if nxt.kind == "op" and nxt.value == "(":
713	            if tok.kind == "ident" and tok.value.lower() in _AGG_NAMES:
714	                raise QueryValidationError(
715	                    f"aggregate functions must not be nested: "
716	                    f"{func.upper()}({tok.value.upper()}(...))"
717	                )
718	            raise QuerySyntaxError(
719	                f"{func.upper()} argument must be a column name, not a function call"
720	            )
721	        self._reject_expression_in_agg_arg(func)
722	        return (tok.value, None, False)
723	
724	    def _reject_expression_in_agg_arg(self, func: str) -> None:
725	        # Aggregate arguments stay limited to plain column references; a
726	        # scalar expression inside an aggregate query is a validation error.
727	        if self._arith_op_ahead():
728	            raise QueryValidationError(
729	                f"{func.upper()} argument must be a column reference, not an expression"
730	            )
731	
732	    def _parse_limit(self) -> int:
733	        tok = self._peek()
734	        if (
735	            tok.kind != "number"
736	            or isinstance(tok.value, bool)
737	            or not isinstance(tok.value, int)
738	        ):
739	            raise QuerySyntaxError("LIMIT requires an unsigned integer literal")
740	        self._next()
741	        if not (0 <= tok.value <= 2**63 - 1):
742	            raise QuerySyntaxError(
743	                f"LIMIT value {tok.value} is outside the allowed range"
744	            )
745	        return tok.value
746	
747	    def _expect_table_name(self) -> _Token:
748	        tok = self._peek()
749	        if tok.kind in ("ident", "qident"):
750	            return self._next()
751	        raise QuerySyntaxError(f"expected table name, got {tok.text!r}")
752	
753	    def _parse_group_name(self) -> tuple:
754	        # Returns a (table|None, table_quoted, name) triple.
755	        tok = self._peek()
756	        if tok.kind == "keyword" and tok.value == "case":
757	            raise QueryValidationError(
758	                "GROUP BY only accepts column references, not CASE expressions"
759	            )
760	        if tok.kind not in ("ident", "qident"):
761	            raise QuerySyntaxError(f"expected identifier, got {tok.text!r}")
762	        if self._allow_join and self._qualifier_ahead():
763	            item = self._parse_qualified_column()
764	            result = (item.table, item.table_quoted, item.name)
765	        else:
766	            self._next()
767	            result = (None, False, tok.value)
768	        # GROUP BY keeps accepting column references only; a scalar
769	        # expression in an aggregate query is a validation error.
770	        if self._arith_op_ahead():
771	            raise QueryValidationError(
772	                "GROUP BY only accepts column references, not expressions"
773	            )
774	        return result

776	    # WHERE expression grammar ------------------------------------------------
777	
778	    def _parse_or(self) -> tuple:
779	        node = self._parse_and()
780	        while self._accept_keyword("or"):
781	            node = ("or", node, self._parse_and())
782	        return node
783	
784	    def _parse_and(self) -> tuple:
785	        node = self._parse_comparison()
786	        while self._accept_keyword("and"):
787	            node = ("and", node, self._parse_comparison())
788	        return node
789	
790	    def _parse_comparison(self) -> tuple:
791	        left = self._parse_not_factor()
792	        tok = self._peek()
793	        if tok.kind == "op" and tok.value in self._CMP_OPS:
794	            self._next()
795	            right = self._parse_not_factor()
796	            return ("cmp", tok.value, left, right)
797	        return left
798	
799	    def _parse_not_factor(self) -> tuple:
800	        if self._accept_keyword("not"):
801	            return ("not", self._parse_not_factor())
802	        return self._parse_postfix()
803	
804	    def _parse_postfix(self) -> tuple:
805	        node = self._parse_arith()
806	        if self._accept_keyword("is"):
807	            negate = self._accept_keyword("not")
808	            self._expect_keyword("null")
809	            node = ("isnull", node, negate)
810	        return node
811	
812	    # Arithmetic expressions (numeric scalar operands) ------------------------
813	    # Precedence (highest first): parentheses, unary +/-, * /, + -.
814	
815	    def _parse_arith(self) -> tuple:
816	        node = self._parse_term()
817	        while True:
818	            tok = self._peek()
819	            if tok.kind == "op" and tok.value in ("+", "-"):
820	                self._next()
821	                node = ("arith", tok.value, node, self._parse_term())
822	            else:
823	                return node
824	
825	    def _parse_term(self) -> tuple:
826	        node = self._parse_factor()
827	        while True:
828	            tok = self._peek()
829	            if tok.kind == "star":
830	                self._next()
831	                node = ("arith", "*", node, self._parse_factor())
832	            elif tok.kind == "op" and tok.value == "/":
833	                self._next()
834	                node = ("arith", "/", node, self._parse_factor())
835	            else:
836	                return node
837	
838	    def _parse_factor(self) -> tuple:
839	        tok = self._peek()
840	        if tok.kind == "op" and tok.value in ("+", "-"):
841	            negate = tok.value == "-"
842	            self._next()
843	            nxt = self._peek()
844	            if nxt.kind == "number" and not isinstance(nxt.value, bool):
845	                # A signed numeric literal is folded at parse time so the
846	                # signed int64 range check keeps its historical meaning
847	                # (-9223372036854775808 is valid, the bare magnitude is not).
848	                self._next()
849	                value = nxt.value
850	                if isinstance(value, int):
851	                    if negate:
852	                        value = -value
853	                    if not (-(2**63) <= value <= 2**63 - 1):
854	                        raise QuerySyntaxError(
855	                            "integer literal is outside the int64 range"
856	                        )
857	                    return ("literal", value, "int64")
858	                if negate:
859	                    value = -value
860	                return ("literal", value, "float64")
861	            if nxt.kind not in ("ident", "qident") and not (
862	                nxt.kind == "op" and nxt.value == "("
863	            ) and not (nxt.kind == "keyword" and nxt.value == "case"):
864	                raise QuerySyntaxError(
865	                    "sign must be followed by a numeric literal or expression"
866	                )
867	            return ("unary", self._parse_factor(), negate)
868	        node = self._parse_atom()
869	        if (
870	            node[0] == "literal"
871	            and isinstance(node[1], int)
872	            and not isinstance(node[1], bool)
873	            and node[1] > 2**63 - 1
874	        ):
875	            # The magnitude 2**63 is only reachable through an explicit
876	            # negation; a bare literal must fit the signed int64 range.
877	            raise QuerySyntaxError("integer literal is outside the int64 range")
878	        return node
879	
880	    def _parse_atom(self) -> tuple:
881	        if self._accept_op("("):
882	            node = self._parse_or()
883	            self._expect_op(")")
884	            return node
885	        if self._accept_keyword("case"):
886	            return self._parse_case()
887	        tok = self._peek()
888	        if tok.kind == "number":
889	            self._next()
890	            value = tok.value
891	            if isinstance(value, bool):
892	                return ("literal", value, "bool")
893	            type_name = "int64" if isinstance(value, int) else "float64"
894	            return ("literal", value, type_name)
895	        if tok.kind == "string":
896	            self._next()
897	            return ("literal", tok.value, "utf8")
898	        if tok.kind in ("ident", "qident"):
899	            if self._allow_join and self._qualifier_ahead():
900	                item = self._parse_qualified_column()
901	                return ("column", item.name, item.table, item.table_quoted)
902	            nxt = self.tokens[self.pos + 1]
903	            if (
904	                tok.kind == "ident"
905	                and tok.value.lower() in _AGG_NAMES
906	                and nxt.kind == "op"
907	                and nxt.value == "("
908	            ):
909	                raise QueryValidationError(
910	                    f"aggregate {tok.value.upper()}(...) is not allowed here"
911	                )
912	            self._next()
913	            return ("column", tok.value, None, False)
914	        if tok.kind == "keyword":
915	            raise QuerySyntaxError(f"unexpected keyword {tok.text.upper()!r} in expression")
916	        raise QuerySyntaxError(f"unexpected token {tok.text!r} in expression")
917	
918	    def _parse_case(self) -> tuple:
919	        # A searched CASE: at least one "WHEN cond THEN result", an optional
920	        # "ELSE result", terminated by END.  Conditions are boolean
921	        # expressions; results are scalar (numeric, bool or utf8) and may
922	        # themselves contain nested CASE expressions.  The simple form
923	        # (CASE value WHEN ...) is not supported.
924	        branches: list[tuple] = []
925	        while True:
926	            self._expect_keyword("when")
927	            condition = self._parse_or()
928	            self._expect_keyword("then")
929	            result = self._parse_arith()
930	            branches.append((condition, result))
931	            tok = self._peek()
932	            if not (tok.kind == "keyword" and tok.value == "when"):
933	                break
934	        else_node = None
935	        if self._accept_keyword("else"):
936	            else_node = self._parse_arith()
937	        self._expect_keyword("end")
938	        return ("case", tuple(branches), else_node)
939	
940	    # Token helpers -----------------------------------------------------------
941	
942	    def _peek(self) -> _Token:
943	        return self.tokens[self.pos]
944	
945	    def _next(self) -> _Token:
946	        tok = self.tokens[self.pos]
947	        self.pos += 1
948	        return tok
949	
950	    def _accept(self, kind: str) -> bool:
951	        if self._peek().kind == kind:
952	            self.pos += 1
953	            return True
954	        return False
955	
956	    def _accept_op(self, value: str) -> bool:
957	        tok = self._peek()
958	        if tok.kind == "op" and tok.value == value:
959	            self.pos += 1
960	            return True
961	        return False
962	
963	    def _accept_keyword(self, value: str) -> bool:
964	        tok = self._peek()
965	        if tok.kind == "keyword" and tok.value == value:
966	            self.pos += 1
967	            return True
968	        return False
969	
970	    def _expect_keyword(self, value: str) -> _Token:
971	        tok = self._peek()
972	        if tok.kind != "keyword" or tok.value != value:
973	            raise QuerySyntaxError(f"expected {value.upper()}, got {tok.text!r}")
974	        return self._next()
975	
976	    def _expect_op(self, value: str) -> _Token:
977	        tok = self._peek()
978	        if tok.kind != "op" or tok.value != value:
979	            raise QuerySyntaxError(f"expected {value!r}, got {tok.text!r}")
980	        return self._next()

990	    """A validated projection element."""

992	    kind: str  # "column" | "agg" | "expr"
993	    output_name: str
994	    # kind == "column":
995	    col_index: int = -1
996	    # kind == "agg":
997	    func: str = ""
998	    arg_index: int = -1  # -1 means COUNT(*)

1000	    # kind == "expr":
1001	    expr: tuple | None = None  # bound scalar expression
1002	    out_type: str = ""

1006	def _bind_select(select: _Select, schema: Schema, expected_table="input") -> dict:
1007	    if expected_table is not None:
1008	        table_matches = (
1009	            select.table == expected_table
1010	            if select.table_quoted
1011	            else select.table.lower() == expected_table.lower()
1012	        )
1013	        if not table_matches:
1014	            raise QueryValidationError(
1015	                f"unknown table {select.table!r}; only {expected_table!r} is supported"
1016	            )
1017	
1018	    where = _bind_expr(select.where, schema) if select.where is not None else None
1019	    if where is not None and where[0] in (
1020	        "literal",
1021	        "column",
1022	        "arith",
1023	        "unary",
1024	        "case",
1025	    ):
1026	        type_name = _expr_type(where)
1027	        if type_name != "bool":
1028	            raise QueryValidationError(
1029	                f"WHERE clause must be boolean, got {type_name}"
1030	            )
1031	
1032	    if not select.is_aggregate_query:
1033	        return _bind_plain(select, schema, where)
1034	    return _bind_aggregate(select, schema, where)

1037	def _bind_plain(select: _Select, schema: Schema, where) -> dict:
1038	    # Non-aggregate path: '*' or a comma-separated list of plain columns and
1039	    # computed scalar expressions (each named with AS).
1040	    bound_items: list[_BoundItem] = []
1041	    if select.star:

1344	def _bind_expr(node: tuple, schema: Schema) -> tuple:
1345	    tag = node[0]
1346	    if tag == "literal":
1347	        return node
1348	    if tag == "column":
1349	        name = node[1]
1350	        try:
1351	            index = schema.index(name)
1352	        except KeyError:
1353	            raise QueryValidationError(f"unknown column: {name!r}") from None
1354	        col = schema.columns[index]
1355	        return ("column", name, index, col.type, col.nullable)
1356	    if tag == "not":
1357	        operand = _bind_expr(node[1], schema)
1358	        _require_boolean(operand, "NOT")
1359	        return ("not", operand)
1360	    if tag in ("and", "or"):
1361	        left = _bind_expr(node[1], schema)
1362	        right = _bind_expr(node[2], schema)
1363	        _require_boolean(left, tag.upper())
1364	        _require_boolean(right, tag.upper())
1365	        return (tag, left, right)
1366	    if tag == "isnull":
1367	        operand = _bind_expr(node[1], schema)
1368	        if operand[0] not in ("literal", "column", "arith", "unary", "case"):
1369	            raise QuerySyntaxError(
1370	                "IS NULL operand must be a column reference or a literal"
1371	            )
1372	        return ("isnull", operand, node[2])
1373	    if tag == "unary":
1374	        operand = _bind_expr(node[1], schema)
1375	        type_name = _expr_type(operand)
1376	        if type_name not in ("int64", "float64"):
1377	            raise QueryValidationError(
1378	                f"unary +/- requires a numeric operand, got {type_name}"
1379	            )
1380	        return ("unary", operand, node[2], type_name)
1381	    if tag == "arith":
1382	        left = _bind_expr(node[2], schema)
1383	        right = _bind_expr(node[3], schema)
1384	        left_t = _expr_type(left)
1385	        right_t = _expr_type(right)
1386	        if left_t not in ("int64", "float64") or right_t not in ("int64", "float64"):
1387	            raise QueryValidationError(
1388	                f"arithmetic requires numeric operands, got {left_t} and {right_t}"
1389	            )
1390	        op = node[1]
1391	        out_type = (
1392	            "float64"
1393	            if op == "/" or "float64" in (left_t, right_t)
1394	            else "int64"
1395	        )
1396	        return ("arith", op, left, right, out_type)
1397	    if tag == "case":
1398	        bound_branches = []
1399	        result_types: list[str] = []
1400	        for cond_node, result_node in node[1]:
1401	            cond = _bind_expr(cond_node, schema)
1402	            _require_boolean(cond, "WHEN")
1403	            result = _bind_expr(result_node, schema)
1404	            bound_branches.append((cond, result))
1405	            result_types.append(_expr_type(result))
1406	        else_bound = None
1407	        if node[2] is not None:
1408	            else_bound = _bind_expr(node[2], schema)
1409	            result_types.append(_expr_type(else_bound))
1410	        out_type = _unify_case_types(result_types)
1411	        return ("case", tuple(bound_branches), else_bound, out_type)
1412	    if tag == "cmp":
1413	        op = node[1]
1414	        left = _bind_expr(node[2], schema)
1415	        right = _bind_expr(node[3], schema)
1416	        if left[0] not in (
1417	            "literal", "column", "arith", "unary", "case"
1418	        ) or right[0] not in ("literal", "column", "arith", "unary", "case"):
1419	            raise QuerySyntaxError("comparison operands must be column references or literals")
1420	        left_t = _expr_type(left)
1421	        right_t = _expr_type(right)
1422	        if "bool" in (left_t, right_t):
1423	            if left_t != "bool" or right_t != "bool":
1424	                raise QueryValidationError(
1425	                    f"bool can only be compared to bool, got {left_t} and {right_t}"
1426	                )
1427	            if op not in ("=", "!="):
1428	                raise QueryValidationError(f"bool only supports = and !=, not {op!r}")

1442	def _unify_case_types(types: list[str]) -> str:
1443	    """Unify the static types of every reachable CASE result.
1444	
1445	    int64 and float64 may mix and unify to float64; bool and utf8 must
1446	    match every other result exactly.  Anything else is incompatible.
1447	    """
1448	    unique = set(types)
1449	    if unique <= {"int64", "float64"}:
1450	        return "float64" if "float64" in unique else "int64"
1451	    if len(unique) == 1:
1452	        return next(iter(unique))
1453	    raise QueryValidationError(
1454	        "CASE results must have consistent types: "
1455	        + ", ".join(sorted(unique))
1456	    )

1460	    """The static type of a bound value node."""
1461	    tag = node[0]
1462	    if tag == "literal":
1463	        return node[2]
1464	    if tag == "column":
1465	        return node[3]
1466	    if tag == "unary":
1467	        return node[3]
1468	    if tag == "arith":
1469	        return node[4]
1470	    if tag == "case":
1471	        return node[3]

1475	def _expr_nullable(node: tuple) -> bool:
1476	    """Whether a bound value node can yield NULL (derived from its columns)."""
1477	    tag = node[0]
1478	    if tag == "literal":
1479	        return False
1480	    if tag == "column":
1481	        return node[4]
1482	    if tag == "unary":
1483	        return _expr_nullable(node[1])
1484	    if tag == "arith":
1485	        return _expr_nullable(node[2]) or _expr_nullable(node[3])
1486	    if tag == "case":
1487	        # The value is NULL only when a reachable result yields NULL, or
1488	        # every WHEN fails/UNKNOWN and no ELSE was given (implicit NULL).
1489	        # A NULL condition merely routes the row elsewhere and never makes
1490	        # a non-NULL result nullable.
1491	        if node[2] is None:
1492	            return True
1493	        return any(_expr_nullable(result) for _cond, result in node[1]) or _expr_nullable(
1494	            node[2]
1495	        )
1496	    raise QuerySyntaxError(f"unsupported expression: {tag}")  # pragma: no cover - defensive

1503	    if type_name != "bool":

1512	def _eval(node: tuple, row: tuple) -> bool | None:
1513	    tag = node[0]
1514	    if tag == "literal":
1515	        return node[1]
1516	    if tag == "column":
1517	        return row[node[2]]
1518	    if tag == "unary":
1519	        value = _eval(node[1], row)
1520	        if value is None:
1521	            return None
1522	        if not node[2]:  # unary plus keeps the value
1523	            return value
1524	        return _negate_value(value)
1525	    if tag == "arith":
1526	        left = _eval(node[2], row)
1527	        right = _eval(node[3], row)
1528	        if left is None or right is None:
1529	            return None
1530	        return _arith_value(node[1], left, right)
1531	    if tag == "case":
1532	        # Conditions are tried in written order; only TRUE matches.  FALSE
1533	        # and UNKNOWN fall through, so unhit results are never evaluated:
1534	        # their division-by-zero, int64 overflow or non-finite float64
1535	        # cannot raise.  The chosen result alone is evaluated.
1536	        for condition, result in node[1]:
1537	            if _eval(condition, row) is True:
1538	                value = _eval(result, row)
1539	                break
1540	        else:
1541	            value = None if node[2] is None else _eval(node[2], row)
1542	        if value is None:
1543	            return None
1544	        # int64/float64 results unify to float64; ints become floats.
1545	        if node[3] == "float64" and isinstance(value, int) and not isinstance(value, bool):
1546	            return float(value)
1547	        return value
1548	    if tag == "isnull":
1549	        value = _eval(node[1], row)
1550	        result = value is None
1551	        return (not result) if node[2] else result
1552	    if tag == "not":
1553	        value = _eval(node[1], row)
1554	        return None if value is None else (not value)
1555	    if tag in ("and", "or"):
1556	        # Short-circuit SQL semantics; UNKNOWN propagates only when needed.
1557	        if tag == "and":
1558	            left = _eval(node[1], row)
1559	            if left is False:
1560	                return False
1561	            right = _eval(node[2], row)
1562	            if right is False:
1563	                return False
1564	            if left is None or right is None:
1565	                return None
1566	            return True
1567	        left = _eval(node[1], row)
1568	        if left is True:
1569	            return True
1570	        right = _eval(node[2], row)
1571	        if right is True:
1572	            return True
1573	        if left is None or right is None:
1574	            return None
1575	        return False
1576	    if tag == "cmp":
1577	        left = _eval(node[2], row)
1578	        right = _eval(node[3], row)
1579	        if left is None or right is None:
1580	            return None
1581	        op = node[1]
1582	        if op == "=":
1583	            result = left == right
1584	        elif op == "!=":
1585	            result = left != right
1586	        elif op == "<":
1587	            result = left < right
1588	        elif op == "<=":
1589	            result = left <= right
1590	        elif op == ">":
1591	            result = left > right
1592	        else:  # ">="
1593	            result = left >= right
1594	        return bool(result)
1595	    raise QuerySyntaxError(f"unsupported expression: {tag}")  # pragma: no cover

1600	    if isinstance(value, int):
1601	        if value == _INT64_MIN:
1602	            raise QueryValidationError(
1603	                "negating the int64 minimum overflows the int64 range"
1604	            )
1605	        return -value
